-- (native ob3ect designer; elaborate against the kernel to verify)
name: fifth run meta-description → verdict N · closure false
notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

fifth run meta-description → verdict N · closure false · topology flat_chain · steps 14

phase_0.boundary_condition: the meta-evaluation frame that contains the fifth run's self-description and its structural verdict
phase_0.domain_name: fifth run meta-description → verdict N · closure false
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: pulls the declared values — verdict N, closure false, topology flat_chain, steps 14 — into the evaluation frame

AREV.justification: descends from the structured description back to the uninterpreted sequence of fourteen steps

CLINK.justification: chains the forward pull of parameters with the backward descent to the raw steps, forming a single traversal

ENGAGR.chosen_element: simultaneous hold of topology match and mismatch
ENGAGR.justification: the run's own meta-description claims flat_chain while the step trace may contain hidden branching; both states are kept live without collapse

EVALF.justification: the negative arm where a fork or fuse is detected in the fourteen steps, falsifying the flat_chain assertion

EVALT.justification: the affirmative arm where the step sequence exhibits no FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs and no nesting

FFUSE.chosen_element: rejoin of topology and length arms
FFUSE.justification: the two arms fuse into a single structural verdict; if they conflict the join yields B, if both hold it yields T, if neither it yields N

FSPLIT.justification: splits evaluation into two arms: one checking whether the topology is genuinely flat_chain, the other checking whether the step count matches the claimed length

IFIX.justification: permanently records the structural assessment of the fifth run's self-description in the immutable run history

IMSCRIB.justification: the description identifies itself as the object it describes, a neutral identity anchor

TANCH.justification: the completed description of the fifth run is fixed as a closed object for inspection

VINIT.justification: no run data has been inscribed; the buffer holds neither structure nor verdict

phase_2.fuse_element: rejoin of topology and length arms
phase_2.fuse_result: a single structural verdict on whether the fifth run's self-description is topologically faithful
phase_2.rejoin_note: the topology arm checks for forks in the step trace; the length arm counts steps; they rejoin after both checks complete — the fork closes because both arms perform concrete work on the extracted parameters
phase_2.split_input: the extracted run parameters including topology flat_chain and steps 14
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: the meta-description asserts flat_chain while the trace evidence simultaneously supports and contradicts it, a live structural contradiction
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10) — constructively refuted: a fork or fuse is found in the trace, or the step count diverges from fourteen
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01) — constructively proven: the fourteen-step trace contains no FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs and the step count matches exactly
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: the meta-description buffer is empty, no run structure has been loaded

steps.domain_action: extract run parameters — verdict N, closure false, topology flat_chain, steps 14
branch on topology claim into topology-check arm and step-count arm
topology-check arm confirms no forks or fuses in the fourteen steps
topology-check arm detects a fork or fuse in the step trace
step-count arm advances through each of the fourteen steps
step-count arm retracts to verify total count equals fourteen
hold both topology confirmation and topology contradiction simultaneously
rejoin topology and step-count arms into single structural verdict
compose extraction, split, evaluation, and fuse into one meta-evaluation traversal
seal the meta-description record as closed object

phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical run archive containing all prior run records and their meta-descriptions
phase_5.compiler_frontend: the meta-evaluator that parses run declarations into structured parameters
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: parameter passing between extraction, split arms, and fuse via the evaluation frame
phase_5.memory_mechanism: run ledger storing immutable meta-verdicts appended by IFIX
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: sequential executor that runs the fourteen-step trace, then the meta-evaluation sequence

phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the meta-evaluation extracts, checks, and fixes information without discarding or duplicating structural content; the ledger grows by one fixed record per cycle
phase_6.post_cycle_state: run ledger contains five sealed meta-verdicts; fifth run trace is archived
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: run ledger contains four sealed meta-verdicts; fifth run trace sits in raw buffer
